VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The Luhn logic is in the wrong unit. This codebase already has an established, visible pattern for non-trivial derived values, and the new method breaks from it while sitting right next to two examples of it.

Findings:

1. **Extract the algorithm to a utility class under `rest.function.common`, matching `Localities`/`IdentityKey`.** Two of the mappings immediately adjacent to the new one delegate to dedicated final helper classes via fully-qualified expressions:
   - `locality` → `...rest.function.common.Localities.of(...)` (`OwnerMapper.java:26-28`)
   - `identityKey` → `...rest.function.owner.IdentityKey.ofOwner(owner)` (`OwnerMapper.java:34-36`)

   A self-contained ~20-line algorithm (digit crunch + Luhn doubling) is exactly the kind of logic those classes exist to hold. It should be a `Luhn` class in `rest.function.common` with a `static int checkDigit(String)`, referenced as `java(...common.Luhn.checkDigit(owner.getCustomerCode()))` — consistent with `locality` two lines above.

2. **`OwnerMapper` is becoming a catch-all.** The existing `default` methods in this interface are either trivial mapping predicates (`hasEmail`, `OwnerMapper.java:45-48`) or MapStruct assembly plumbing (`toOwnerPageDto`, `OwnerMapper.java:82-90`). Neither is a general algorithm. Adding a reusable check-digit routine here mixes domain algorithm code into a mapping interface — the very concern the `common` package was created to keep out. A maintainer looking for the Luhn routine would expect it beside `Localities`, not buried as a mapper default.

The OpenAPI addition and the algorithm itself read fine; the only issue is placement/consistency.
